## The implicit operator and its sparse system (`build_implicit_operator`, `SparseSystemMatrix`) {#sec-ch09-assembly}

### Summary

All implicit steps of the solver need the same object: the linear operator $\mathsf L = \mathsf T + \mathsf J$ of
transport plus linearized sources, on the flattened state of every cell and species, combined with a multiple of the
identity. This section describes how that operator is assembled as one sparse matrix, how the backward-Euler system is
formed from it, and how it is solved on CPU and on CUDA.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** $\mathsf L = \mathsf T + \mathsf J$ and the backward-Euler system @eq-ch09-assembly-be.

**Data.** Flattened state of `ncol*nlyr*nspecies` unknowns; sparse CSR[^rg-1ad56b80a4ed] matrix; right side `(ncol, nlyr, nspecies)`.

**Placement.** Built once per Rosenbrock step or Newton iteration (@sec-ch09-rosenbrock, @sec-ch09-newton).

**Activation.** API: `build_implicit_operator`, `build_implicit_step_system`, `solve_sparse_system`.

**Guarantee / limits.** Exact assembly; direct sparse solve (SciPy on CPU, cuSolver on CUDA).

**Evidence.** See the Tests layer.
:::

Local symbols: $\mathsf L$, the operator; $\mathsf T$, transport (@sec-ch09-transport); $\mathsf J$, block-diagonal
source Jacobian (@sec-ch09-sources); $\mathsf I$, identity; $\Delta t$, step; $c^{0}$, the state at the start of the
step; $c^{k}$, the current Newton iterate.

### Derivation

Backward Euler for $\mathrm d c/\mathrm d t = \mathsf T c + S(c)$, with the source linearized about $c^{k}$,
$S(c) \approx S(c^{k}) + \mathsf J (c - c^{k})$, gives for the new state $c$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
c - c^{0} &= \Delta t \left[\mathsf T c + S(c^{k}) + \mathsf J (c - c^{k})\right], \\
\left(\mathsf I - \Delta t\, \mathsf L\right) c &= c^{0} + \Delta t \left[S(c^{k}) - \mathsf J c^{k}\right] .
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch09-assembly-be}

`build_implicit_step_system` ({{< code python/atm2d/assembly.py build_implicit_step_system >}}) returns this matrix
and right side when $\Delta t < 1$, and the same system divided by $\Delta t$,
$(\mathsf I/\Delta t - \mathsf L) c = c^{0}/\Delta t + S(c^{k}) - \mathsf J c^{k}$, when $\Delta t \ge 1$ (in the
caller's time unit). The two have the same solution in exact arithmetic; the switch keeps the matrix entries of order
one or of order $\lVert \mathsf L \rVert$ rather than $\Delta t \lVert \mathsf L \rVert$. A non-local source operator,
if any, is added to $\mathsf J$ in both the matrix and the term $\mathsf J c^{k}$.

### Numerical method

`build_implicit_operator` ({{< code python/atm2d/assembly.py build_implicit_operator >}}) adds the cell-local blocks
(kinetics, photochemistry, source terms, and $\mathsf I/\Delta t$ if requested) to the transport matrix as diagonal
blocks, then adds any non-local operator and, last, the boundary rows of @sec-ch09-transport.
`SparseSystemMatrix.affine_with_identity` forms $a\,\mathsf I + b\,\mathsf L$ in coordinate form without densifying.
`solve_sparse_system` ({{< code python/atm2d/solver.py solve_sparse_system >}}) applies the right-side overrides of
boundary rows, then solves directly: on CPU with a SciPy factorization cached on the matrix object (so the two solves
of a Rosenbrock step share it), on CUDA with the native cuSolver CSR binding.

The assembly figure is not provided: the figure module is not written yet.

| what | code link | symbol | switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| operator | {{< code python/atm2d/assembly.py build_implicit_operator >}} | `build_implicit_operator` | `kinetics`, `photo_chem`, `source_terms` |
| backward-Euler system | {{< code python/atm2d/assembly.py build_implicit_step_system >}} | `build_implicit_step_system` | `dt` |
| sparse matrix | {{< code python/atm2d/matrix.py SparseSystemMatrix >}} | `SparseSystemMatrix` | API |
| $a\mathsf I + b\mathsf L$ | {{< code python/atm2d/matrix.py SparseSystemMatrix.affine_with_identity >}} | `affine_with_identity` | always |
| boundary rows | {{< code python/atm2d/matrix.py SparseSystemMatrix.replace_rows >}} | `replace_rows` | boundary conditions |
| solve | {{< code python/atm2d/solver.py solve_sparse_system >}} | `solve_sparse_system` | device |

Setup checks a user can hit: `photo_chem` without `actinic_flux`; `include_identity` without `dt`; diagonal blocks or
a right side of the wrong shape.

### Limits

`build_implicit_step_system` takes no boundary conditions, so a backward-Euler step built with it has no boundary
rows; boundaries must be added by a `system_postprocess` hook or by pins (@sec-ch09-conservation). `affine_with_identity`
does not carry the right-side overrides of an operator that already has boundary rows (verified by reading); no step
path at the pin applies it to such an operator. The threshold $\Delta t = 1$ of the rescaled form is in the caller's
time unit, not a property of the system.
